content: 1. The effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate may be increased when co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as idelalisib, imatinib, isoniazid, itraconazole, ketoconazole, nefazodone, nicardipine, or posaconazole. These drugs inhibit hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism, leading to elevated plasma hormone concentrations. Caution and monitoring are advised. The use of a non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended in such cases. 2. Ivosidenib may decrease the effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. This reduction in hormonal contraceptive concentrations necessitates close monitoring and consideration of alternative contraceptive methods. 3. Lamotrigine levels may be significantly reduced when used concomitantly with combined hormonal contraceptives (CHCs) containing ethinyl estradiol (EE), likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. This interaction may impair seizure control, requiring dosage adjustments of lamotrigine. 4. Lesinurad (DSC) may reduce the effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative or backup contraceptive methods should be used during co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuing the enzyme inducer to maintain contraceptive reliability. 5. Antibiotics such as levofloxacin, metronidazole, minocycline, moxifloxacin, neomycin, nitrofurantoin, ofloxacin, paromomycin, and penicillin VK may decrease the effectiveness of oral hormonal contraceptives by altering intestinal flora. Although the risk of contraceptive failure is low, caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate may increase the levels of midazolam by inhibiting its metabolism. Ethinyl estradiol may also inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Mineral oil may reduce the effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 8. Mitotane, oxcarbazepine, pentobarbital, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone, rifabutin, and rifampin may reduce the effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative or backup contraceptive methods should be used during co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuing the enzyme inducer to ensure contraceptive reliability. 9. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate may reduce the effectiveness of thyroid hormone replacement therapies, such as levothyroxine, liothyronine, and liotrix, by increasing serum thyroxine-binding globulin concentrations. Women on thyroid hormone replacement therapy may require increased doses of thyroid hormone when using CHCs. 10. Lixisenatide (DSC) may reduce the effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by delaying gastric emptying and inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 11. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate may reduce the effectiveness of lonapegsomatropin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may decrease serum insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-1) response to growth hormone analogs, potentially requiring higher growth hormone doses. 12. Pitolisant may reduce the effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring for reduced effectiveness of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is recommended. 13. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate may increase the levels of prednisolone by inhibiting its metabolism. Combined oral contraceptives containing EE may also inhibit the metabolism of cyclosporine, leading to increased plasma concentrations. Caution and monitoring are advised.
